description: Cash or Crash, a signed cash-out after the first pick survived: the PlayerCashOut EIP-712 message of the round in snapshot/valid/cashorcrash-cash-out-active-step1 (its domain, its roundId as round, and as previous T_1, the structHash of the pick in snapshot/typed-data/cashorcrash-pick, which chains on the round's readyHash T_0), whose typedData is snapshot/typed-data/cashorcrash-cash-out, signed by the round's action key. structHash is T_2. The hashes, digest and signature were made with Foundry cast alone (generatedWith), not with the engine's own EIP-712 code, so a shell that reproduces them agrees with an independent signer. testKey is a public test key: never use it for anything of value.
encodeType: PlayerCashOut(string action,uint8[] path,uint32 sequence,bytes32 round,bytes32 previous)

testKey.note: TEST KEY ONLY. The well-known account at index 3 of the default anvil and Hardhat test mnemonic, public by design; never fund it or use it outside tests. Its address is the round's actionKey.

generatedWith.input: player-cash-out.json holds the eip712 member of this vector.
commands: cast keccak 'PlayerCashOut(string action,uint8[] path,uint32 sequence,bytes32 round,bytes32 previous)'

cast keccak $(cast abi-encode 'f(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,uint256,address)' $(cast keccak 'EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)') $(cast keccak SuperEngine) $(cast keccak 1) 31337 0x5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e5e)

cast keccak $(cast abi-encode 'f(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,uint32,bytes32,bytes32)' 0x4fcc4e30bede285e8cd1551115aee2f18030095285175588103a130a1b118c04 $(cast keccak 'cash out') $(cast keccak $(cast abi-encode 'f(uint8)' 0)) 2 0x01927c5f1a2b7c3d8e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f00000000000000000000000000000000 0x120e27acfca41d0da897bbfab40a7b70d5360d172d3e15d15736ef0be5bec9be)
generatedWith.outputs: The commands print, in order: the address (EIP-55 cased), typeHash, domainSeparator, structHash, digest, and the signature twice. Both signing commands print the same signature, so cast's own EIP-712 digest of the input equals digest. The path [0] is hashed as the keccak256 of its one element's 32-byte encoding, abi-encode of f(uint8) 0.
